author: claude
headline: Calm week at UK and North European ports: a good window to clear releases
standfirst: No weather disruption is forecast at any of the eight ports we track, so push releases and deliveries through now. On the way in, Atlantic arrivals into the Channel may run up to 1 day late. August reliability: Sea-Intelligence 49.9%, Xeneta 29%.

port_notes.felixstowe: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. Speak to your carrier about release and delivery now and book haulage slots while the weather holds.
port_notes.southampton: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. A good week to clear releases: confirm delivery dates with your carrier and haulier now.
port_notes.london_gateway: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. Speak to your carrier about release now and lock in weekend haulage while slots are easy to get.

port_notes.rotterdam: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. If you tranship via Rotterdam, confirm your feeder connection now while conditions are settled.
port_notes.antwerp: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. Speak to your carrier about release and onward delivery now.
port_notes.bremerhaven: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. Speak to your carrier about release and feeder connections now.
port_notes.hamburg: Monday's wind risk has eased in the latest forecast, and no limits are now expected. Speak to your carrier about release now.

inbound_note: Two lanes may slow arrivals. Seas of 4.9 m in the Western Approaches on Thursday could push transatlantic and Cape-routed Asia arrivals into the Channel up to 1 day late. Off the Cape, 4 m seas on Tuesday 6 October may add up to 1 day to Asia–North Europe services routed that way. Don't book haulage against the published ETA; confirm the revised ETA with your carrier.

sections.ports: A quiet week on the quayside. No port we track is forecast to reach crane or pilotage limits in the next six days. Hamburg's Monday wind risk from this morning's run has faded, with peak gusts revised down from 15.2 m/s to 11.9 m/s. Congestion figures are not yet connected, so each status reflects weather and port news only.
sections.lanes: Only two lanes reach watch level, both for sea state rather than wind, and neither is expected to last more than a day.
sections.reliability: Sea-Intelligence puts August global schedule reliability at 49.9%, down 5.9 pp on July and 15.2 pp on a year ago, with late vessels arriving 6.81 days behind schedule on average. Xeneta measures 29%, down 4 pp. The 20.9 pp gap is methodology, not error: Sea-Intelligence counts an arrival as on time within one day of schedule, while Xeneta counts only arrivals on the scheduled day. Both put Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd first and second. For planning, assume roughly half of arrivals will miss their scheduled day and leave slack in delivery promises.
sections.advisories: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd plan to resume Suez Canal routing on the AE12 service from 27 October, and Hapag-Lloyd is reported to be restoring Suez transits on its India to US East Coast service. Surcharges keep building: Maersk peak season surcharges on South America to Europe (USD 500) and Europe to South Africa, a CMA CGM reefer surcharge from South America to North Europe, and new FAK rates from MSC and CMA CGM. Peel Ports has reinstated a weekly Greenock to Rotterdam service.
